sentences.zh: 而且，呃，其中一个人不知为什么看着眼熟。

sentences.en: This lady looked very familiar.
sentences.zh: 这位女士看着非常眼熟。

sentences.en: Like, where did I know her from?
sentences.zh: 我就想，我是在哪儿见过她呢？

sentences.en: And that lady that I recognized was the same lady that came and brought the weed from me.
sentences.zh: 我认出的那个女人，就是之前来我这儿买大麻的那个女人。

sentences.en: Like, is Julius Irving here?
sentences.zh: 就像是，朱利叶斯·欧文在这儿吗？

sentences.en: I stepped outside real quick and closed the door.
sentences.zh: 我迅速走到外面，把门关上了。

sentences.en: All this weed aroma coming out the house.
sentences.zh: 满屋子都是大麻的香味飘出来。

sentences.en: And I was like, uh, I'm like, yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 然后我就说，呃，我说，在的，长官。

sentences.en: I'm Julius Irving.
sentences.zh: 我就是朱利叶斯·欧文。

sentences.en: And, uh, we have a warrant for your arreSt.
sentences.zh: 然后，呃，我们有对你的逮捕令。

sentences.en: This part of Julius's story is a little less typical.
sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯这段经历有点不太典型。

sentences.en: This was back in 2005.
sentences.zh: 那是2005年的事。

sentences.en: At the time, there was a popular TV show in Gainesville called Gainesville Police Beat.
sentences.zh: 当时，盖恩斯维尔有一档很受欢迎的电视节目叫《盖恩斯维尔警务实录》。

sentences.en: It was like a local version of the show Cops.
sentences.zh: 它有点像地方版的《缉毒风云》。

sentences.en: But this particular show was produced by the police department itself.
sentences.zh: 但这个特定的节目是由警察局自己制作的。

sentences.en: So that's who showed up at Julius's door that day, the police and the camera crew, to capture footage of him being arrested to later air on the episode.
sentences.zh: 所以那天出现在朱利叶斯门前的就是他们，警察和摄像团队，为了拍摄他被捕的画面好在节目中播出。

sentences.en: Welcome to Police Beat.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看《警务实录》。

sentences.en: My name is Keith Kamig, and I'm the spokesperson for the Gainesville police department.
sentences.zh: 我是基思·卡米格，盖恩斯维尔警察局的新闻发言人。

sentences.en: Did other people see the TV show?
sentences.zh: 其他人也看过这个电视节目吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，看过。

sentences.en: At the time, it was, it was like, I don't even think the show still runs anymore.
sentences.zh: 当时，它，我觉得现在这节目可能都不播了。

sentences.en: But, uh, at the time, it was pretty popular in Gainesville.
sentences.zh: 但是，呃，当时在盖恩斯维尔挺受欢迎的。

sentences.en: Like, oh, we got our own, we're the cops here in Gainesville, Florida, so everybody watched it and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哦，我们有自己的节目，我们就是佛罗里达州盖恩斯维尔的警察，所以大家都看，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I heard, I heard quite a bit about it after it happened.
sentences.zh: 对，事情发生后，我听说、我听到了不少关于它的议论。

sentences.en: Did anybody explain to you what rights you were gonna lose with a felony charge, with a drug charge?
sentences.zh: 有人向你解释过，背上重罪指控、毒品指控会让你失去哪些权利吗？

sentences.en: Uh, nah, not really, no sir.
sentences.zh: 呃，没有，其实没有，长官。

sentences.en: I don't imagine you were thinking about voting at that point.
sentences.zh: 我想你当时肯定没在考虑投票的事。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: Not even a little bit.
sentences.zh: 一点都没想过。

sentences.en: At that time, voting was probably the farthest thing from my mind.
sentences.zh: 那时候，投票对我来说大概是最遥远的事情了。

sentences.en: Like, I never thought about things like that at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我根本不会去想那种事。

sentences.en: Julius was sentenced to 90 days in jail for selling marijuana to that undercover officer.
sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯因为向那个便衣警察卖大麻被判入狱90天。

sentences.en: And after he got out, he went back to selling drugs.
sentences.zh: 他出来后，又重操旧业开始卖毒品。

sentences.en: I got discreet life, man, heavy.
sentences.zh: 我过着极其隐秘的生活，伙计，非常严重。

sentences.en: You know, I started using harder drugs and everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我开始吸食更硬的毒品之类的。

sentences.en: Uh, and, uh, I never thought about working.
sentences.zh: 呃，而且，呃，我从来没想过要去工作。

sentences.en: I'm like, man, working's some bullshit.
sentences.zh: 我想，老天，工作简直就是扯淡。

sentences.en: Like, like, like, uh, why would I fucking spend eight hours of my life at a place and only giving me, at the time, minimum wage was like, sit something.
sentences.zh: 就像，就像，呃，我他妈凭什么把生命中的八个小时耗在一个地方，当时最低工资好像才六块多。

sentences.en: I sit 75 for an hour of my life.
sentences.zh: 我拿我生命中的一个小时换1.75美元。

sentences.en: I sit in this place and flip these burgers or take out this trash or mop this floor for $6 per hour.
sentences.zh: 我坐在这个地方煎汉堡、倒垃圾或者拖地，一小时就赚6美元。

sentences.en: Hell no, I'd rather hang in the hood and I can make motherfucking $100 an hour.
sentences.zh: 见鬼去吧，我宁愿在街区里闲逛，这样我他妈一小时能赚100块。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: Or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者诸如此类的。

sentences.en: So anyways, um...
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，嗯……

sentences.en: He developed an addiction and ended up in and out of jail over the next couple of years on more drug charges.
sentences.zh: 他染上了毒瘾，在接下来的几年里因为更多毒品罪名频繁进出监狱。

sentences.en: And then he gets a cocaine charge and violates his probation.
sentences.zh: 然后他又摊上了一项可卡因罪名，并且违反了缓刑规定。

sentences.en: And the judge gave me a year and a year, one year and one day in prison.
sentences.zh: 法官判了我一年零一天，在监狱里服刑一年零一天。

sentences.en: Up until this point, Julius had only ever spent time in jail.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，朱利叶斯待过的都只是看守所。

sentences.en: So this was the first time he'd be going to prison.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他第一次真正去监狱服刑。

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是种什么体验？

sentences.en: Now that right there was, uh, it was hurtful, right?
sentences.zh: 那感觉，呃，真的很伤人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they had to get off this bus to ride here and see all of these, like, uh, the fucking gun tower, these tall fences with bob right everywhere.
sentences.zh: 因为他们得从大巴上下来，走到这儿，看到所有这些，呃，该死的枪塔，到处都是带刺铁丝的高墙。

sentences.en: The officers getting off the bus with the shotguns and everything, and us getting off the bus going in.
sentences.zh: 狱警们拿着散弹枪什么的下了车，然后我们下车走进去。

sentences.en: They saying, uh, all right, take off all your clothes.
sentences.zh: 他们说，呃，好了，脱掉所有衣服。

sentences.en: We stand there naked in a room for like 40, 50 men standing there naked.
sentences.zh: 我们在一个房间里赤身裸体地站着，大概有四五十个男人都在那儿赤身裸体。

sentences.en: And then we all get ushered into a room, maybe 10 people at a time.
sentences.zh: 然后我们被带进另一个房间，大概一次10个人。

sentences.en: And there's other officers there and they begin to tell us to do things like, uh, uh, stand up, bend over, put your head, forehead on the bench and spread your butt cheeks.
sentences.zh: 里面还有其他狱警，他们开始命令我们做一些动作，呃，呃，站起来，弯腰，把头、额头贴在长凳上，然后掰开屁股蛋。

sentences.en: As a man, right?
sentences.zh: 作为男人，对吧？

sentences.en: In a room with other men.
sentences.zh: 在一个全都是男人的房间里。

sentences.en: It was like weird feeling for any human being, right?
sentences.zh: 对任何人来说这都是一种诡异的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, unless you experienced it, it's, it's something else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，除非你亲身经历过，否则它是，完全是另一回事。

sentences.en: How did that leave you feeling?
sentences.zh: 那给你留下了什么感受？

sentences.en: Oh, it was just, uh, degrading.
sentences.zh: 哦，这简直就是，呃，人格侮辱。

sentences.en: It was embarrassing on a very, very deep level.
sentences.zh: 这是一种极度、极度深层的羞辱。

sentences.en: I can't explain how embarrassing and how, uh, just weird it was, bro.
sentences.zh: 兄弟，我无法形容那是多么令人尴尬，多么，呃，诡异。

sentences.en: Months into his sentence, Julius says he had an experience that would change him for the worse.
sentences.zh: 服刑几个月后，朱利叶斯说他经历了一件事，这件事彻底改变了他，而且是往坏的方向变。

sentences.en: The way he tells it, a fellow white inmate believed that Julius had stolen some of his remittance money,
sentences.zh: 按他的说法，一名白人狱友认为朱利叶斯偷了他的汇款，

sentences.en: which is money sent to inmates by their families so they can buy specialty foods and items in the prison.
sentences.zh: 也就是家属寄给犯人让他们能在监狱里买特产和物品的钱。

sentences.en: And then one day, Julius says that he was working his job at the prison as a laundromat, handing out clothes to other inmates.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，朱利叶斯说他在监狱的洗衣房工作，负责给其他犯人分发衣服。

sentences.en: So I was doing my laundry thing, duties and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我在干我的洗衣房差事，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: And, uh, while I was inside the laundry room, there's a door that comes from outside of the door that only an officer could open, that any door inside of there with a lock on it,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我在洗衣房里面的时候，外面有一扇门是只有狱警才能打开的，里面任何带锁的门，

sentences.en: only an officer could open or whatever.
sentences.zh: 都只有狱警能打开之类的。

sentences.en: So when I heard the door open behind me, I just assumed that it was the officer coming in.
sentences.zh: 所以当我听到身后的门打开时，我理所当然地以为是狱警进来了。

sentences.en: I didn't initially turn around to look or whatever.
sentences.zh: 一开始我没有转身去看之类的。

sentences.en: Everybody just kept doing my work, kept my head down working.
sentences.zh: 大家都一直在干活，埋头苦干。

sentences.en: So when I heard the door open and close, uh, what was said from the person behind me would turn around.
sentences.zh: 所以当我听到门打开又关上，呃，身后那个人说的话让我转过了身。

sentences.en: It was like, yo, what's up, man?
sentences.zh: 当时他说，哟，最近怎么样，伙计？

sentences.en: Julius alleges that it was a prison guard who allowed the other prisoner into the room to resolve this dispute.
sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯指控说，是一个狱警允许另一个囚犯进入房间来解决这场纠纷。

sentences.en: They opened the door, let him in and closed it.
sentences.zh: 他们打开门，让他进来，然后关上了门。

sentences.en: It was just me and him and there.
sentences.zh: 里面就我和他。

sentences.en: Well, it was like a guard supervising the fight.
sentences.zh: 好吧，就像有个警卫在监督打架一样。

sentences.en: And then after a extended period of time went by, the guard opened the door.
sentences.zh: 然后过了很久之后，警卫打开了门。

sentences.en: They got the dude, he walked out and they told me to clean this shit up and get ready for laundry.
sentences.zh: 他们带走了那家伙，他走了出去，然后他们叫我把这烂摊子收拾干净，准备洗衣服。

sentences.en: So you were in the custody of the state of Florida when this happened to you?
sentences.zh: 所以当你遭遇这些时，你是在佛罗里达州政府的羁押之下？

sentences.en: The custody of the state of Florida, yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州政府的羁押之下，是的，长官。

sentences.en: After that, Julius was assigned to work at a lumber mill under a contract between the prison and a private company that uses prison labor.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，朱利叶斯被指派到一家木材厂工作，这是监狱与一家使用囚犯劳工的私营公司签订的合同项目。

sentences.en: He was paid 25 cents an hour and says he became an agitator at the bill, calling it legalized slavery and encouraging others to quit and protest the low wages.
sentences.zh: 他每小时报酬25美分，他说自己成了厂里的煽动者，称这是合法的奴隶制，并鼓励其他人罢工抗议低工资。

sentences.en: He says one day he reached a breaking point and began just screaming at people.
sentences.zh: 他说有一天他终于到了崩溃的边缘，开始冲着大家尖叫。

sentences.en: He was put in solitary confinement for 30 days where he alleges that he was regularly beaten by the guards.
sentences.zh: 他被关了30天禁闭，他指控自己在那里经常遭到狱警的殴打。

sentences.en: How did this leave you feeling about the state?
sentences.zh: 这让你对政府有什么样的感觉？

sentences.en: It made me feel like the state is worse than any person inside of here.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得政府比这里面的任何一个人都要糟糕。

sentences.en: It made me really start looking at the system in a different kind of way.
sentences.zh: 它让我开始以一种完全不同的眼光来看待这个体制。

sentences.en: Like, you know, like, it's corrupt, it's evil, it's wicked.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，它腐败、邪恶、罪恶。

sentences.en: And it's promoting the same thing as saying that it's trying to stop.
sentences.zh: 它在纵容它宣称要制止的同一种行为。

sentences.en: It's creating more violent versions of people.
sentences.zh: 它在制造更多具有暴力倾向的人。

sentences.en: You know, I went to prison a pretty good dude, bro, but I came home from prison with a chip on my shoulder.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，兄弟，我进监狱时还是个挺不错的家伙，但出狱时我带着满腔的怨恨。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't there like that before.
sentences.zh: 好吧，以前那种感觉没那么强烈。

sentences.en: Did you feel the state was here to protect you at all?
sentences.zh: 你觉得政府在这里有一点点是为了保护你吗？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: Not even a little bit.
sentences.zh: 一点都没有。

sentences.en: There was a time where I believed that, you know, all cops weren't bad.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，我以为，你知道的，并非所有警察都是坏人。

sentences.en: I thought that.
sentences.zh: 我以前是这么想的。

sentences.en: Before this, I came home thinking they're all bad.
sentences.zh: 经历这些之后，我回到家时觉得他们全都是坏人。

sentences.en: They're all bad.
sentences.zh: 他们全都是坏人。

sentences.en: I looked at police now as the biggest gang in the city.
sentences.zh: 我现在把警察看作是这个城市里最大的帮派。

sentences.en: They're the biggest, most organized gang in the city.
sentences.zh: 他们是这个城市里最大、组织最严密的帮派。

sentences.en: You know, and I looked at politicians and people of that nature as like the mob bosses.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我把政客和诸如此类的人看作是黑手党老大。

sentences.en: And the police officers are the other enforcers, you know, because I understood like gang life or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而警察就是他们的执行者，你知道的，因为我懂帮派生活之类的。

sentences.en: And I associated with it.
sentences.zh: 而且我曾同流合污过。

sentences.en: It's the same, it's the same concept.
sentences.zh: 这是同一个道理，完全是同一个概念。

sentences.en: They just do it on a bigger, greater scale.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把规模搞得更大、更宏大而已。

sentences.en: So Julius's prison experience leaves him with a tremendous amount of distrust of the system.
sentences.zh: 所以朱利叶斯的监狱经历让他对这个体制产生了极大的不信任。

sentences.en: But it also activated him in a way that sort of unexpectedly leads him to this kind of work trying to convince people to engage with the system.
sentences.zh: 但这也以某种方式激发了他，出乎意料地引导他做起了这种试图说服人们参与到体制中来的工作。

sentences.en: It starts when he's released in 2009 and eventually gets a job working at Waffle House.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于他2009年出狱后，最终在华夫饼屋找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: When was the first time you heard about Amendment 4?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候第一次听说第四号修正案的？

sentences.en: First time I heard about Amendment 4, I got nominated to go to like a men's retreat because some of the activism work I was doing, like another person.
sentences.zh: 第一次听说第四号修正案，是因为我做的一些激进主义工作，比如另一个人，我被提名去参加一个男士静修会。

sentences.en: What kind of work?
sentences.zh: 什么样的工作？

sentences.en: Oh, just activism work, dealing with guys getting out of prison, helping people get IDs, get like work boots and stuff, get back and forth to work or whatever.
sentences.zh: 哦，就是激进主义工作，处理出狱人员的事，帮人们办身份证，弄工作靴之类的，解决他们上下班交通问题或者别的什么。

sentences.en: And I was doing all of this like out of my own money.
sentences.zh: 而且我做这一切都是自掏腰包。

sentences.en: I was making out of the Waffle House because I was a waiter at the Waffle House and I got pretty good tips.
sentences.zh: 我是靠在华夫饼屋挣的钱，因为我在华夫饼屋当服务员，小费挺不错的。

sentences.en: I make like 150 bucks a day working like five days a week plus whatever my paycheck was when it came.
sentences.zh: 我一周工作五天左右，一天能赚150块钱，再加上发工资时的薪水。

sentences.en: This work Julius is doing catches the attention of a voting rights group which is composed of formerly incarcerated people who are campaigning for Amendment 4 to be passed.
sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯正在做的这项工作引起了一个投票权组织的注意，该组织由曾有服刑经历的人组成，他们正在为第四号修正案的通过而奔走相告。

sentences.en: One of the group's most active members was Julius's own sister who also served time in prison.
sentences.zh: 该组织最活跃的成员之一就是朱利叶斯的亲姐姐，她也曾在监狱服刑。

sentences.en: Together they start going through Gainesville trying to convince people, people mind you who already have the right to vote, to give that right to former felons.
sentences.zh: 他们一起开始在盖恩斯维尔四处奔走，试图说服人们——请注意，这些人本来就已经拥有投票权——把这一权利赋予给曾经的重罪犯。

sentences.en: A little bit of news out of Florida.
sentences.zh: 来自佛罗里达州的一则新闻。

sentences.en: One of the ballot initiatives in Florida that has raised a lot of national attention including statewide effort has been Amendment 4 which would restore voting rights to felons.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州的一项投票提案引起了全国的广泛关注，包括全州范围内的努力，这就是第四号修正案，它将恢复重罪犯的投票权。

sentences.en: This affects over a million potential voters and this is now we've got a projected answer.
sentences.zh: 这影响了超过一百万潜在选民，现在我们有了一个预计的结果。

sentences.en: And they were hugely successful.
sentences.zh: 他们取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Amendment 4 got passed with 65% of Florida voters voting in favor.
sentences.zh: 第四号修正案以65%的佛罗里达州选民赞成票获得通过。

sentences.en: And it was the largest expansion of voting rights in the country in nearly four decades.
sentences.zh: 这是近四十年来美国最大规模的投票权扩大。

sentences.en: I realized through what happened with Amendment 4 that voters collectively when they're on one accord and unified behind any issue can actually change existing law.
sentences.zh: 通过第四号修正案发生的事情，我意识到，选民们只要步调一致、在任何问题上团结起来，就能真正改变现行法律。

sentences.en: Politicians cared enough about what voters had to say if they could collectively get together and say they're in favor of something.
sentences.zh: 政客们其实很在意选民们的诉求，只要选民能齐心协力表达他们支持某事。

sentences.en: They at least put it on the ballot where they can vote on it and then they could possibly change it.
sentences.zh: 他们至少会把它列入选票让大家投票，然后他们就有可能改变它。

sentences.en: So that was like, okay, wow, that's my first time ever seeing any benefit to voting.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的感觉就是，哇，好吧，这是我第一次看到投票带来任何实际好处。

sentences.en: For Julius, the success of Amendment 4 showed him that voting can actually make a difference.
sentences.zh: 对朱利叶斯来说，第四号修正案的成功向他表明，投票确实能带来改变。

sentences.en: It was the first time seeing a positive side to the government that he'd been so skeptical of.
sentences.zh: 这是他第一次看到这个曾让他如此怀疑的政府积极的一面。

sentences.en: That's how he ended up working for an organization that's been trying to register and activate these 1.5 million potential voters.
sentences.zh: 这就是他最终加入一个致力于为这150万潜在选民进行选民登记和动员的组织的原因。

sentences.en: And so as this amendment was finally being applied for the first time in Florida and people were getting their rights back during a presidential election,
sentences.zh: 随着这项修正案终于在佛罗里达州首次实施，人们在总统大选期间重新获得了权利，

sentences.en: we headed out with Julius to watch him register people to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们和朱利叶斯一起出发，看他为人们进行选民登记。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Well, we looked for someone.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们找了一个人。

sentences.en: Why don't you tell us a little bit about how you strategize?
sentences.zh: 你能不能给我们讲讲你是怎么制定策略的？

sentences.zh: 比如说，你在哪里找人，你怎么考虑这一天，去哪里抓人？

sentences.en: I just think about places, you know, where I know a lot of people come, especially people that, you know, I say my intended group of people, my target group of people.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想一些地方，你知道的，我知道很多人会去，尤其是那些，你知道的，我所说的我的目标群体，我的人群目标。

sentences.en: I try to hang places where I know that they'll come, where I'm going to walk around and look for them or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我尽量去我知道他们会去的地方，去那里走走看看他们之类的。

sentences.en: What's your target group of people?
sentences.zh: 你的目标群体是什么人？

sentences.zh: 黑人，你知道的，长得像我的人，像我一样能理解事情的人。

sentences.zh: 还有就是，我了解到非裔美国人和黑人是登记选民中代表性最不足的群体之一。

sentences.en: I just figured it'd be easier for me to, like, meet my quota and my goal by going to the people who I know are, like, stats will show that they're not registered to vote.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，通过去找那些统计数据显示他们没有登记投票的人，我更容易达成我的指标和目标。

sentences.en: So we've come with Julius to the parking lot of a strip mall and we're outside of a plasma donation center just outside of downtown Gainesville.
sentences.zh: 所以我们和朱利叶斯一起来到一个露天购物中心的停车场，我们在盖恩斯维尔市中心外的一个血浆捐献中心外面。

sentences.zh: 这是他登记选民最成功的地方之一。

sentences.zh: 而最低工资只有，你知道的，8.75美元。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，最低工资太烂了。

sentences.en: And half of the jobs, you can't get 40 hours.
sentences.zh: 而且有一半的工作，你都做不到40个小时。

sentences.en: It's just people need money, bro.
sentences.zh: 人们就是需要钱，兄弟。

sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯一开始工作，很快就有几件事变得很清楚。

sentences.zh: 一是他的个人魅力极强。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 另一件事是，他的工作既有对人们的教育意义，也有让他们进行实际登记的意义。

sentences.en: So...

sentences.zh: 曾几何时，我以为他们把这扇门关上了。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯在进行这些对话时真正的优势在于，他要么能与进出血浆中心的人建立联系，要么本身就认识其中的很多人。

sentences.en: I know you.
sentences.zh: 我认识你。

sentences.en: Okay, cool.
sentences.zh: 好的，酷。

sentences.zh: 就像这个人，他是在附近认识的，也是个重罪犯。

sentences.en: So, uh, it's good to specify your race when you do it because of black people, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，当你做这件事的时候，最好明确你的种族，因为黑人群体，对吧？

sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么这很重要。

sentences.en: I could never actually get, you know what I'm saying?

sentences.en: So it's so many reasons you could vote, bro.
sentences.zh: 所以你有很多理由去投票，兄弟。

sentences.zh: 所以这看起来很成功，既教育了这个人关于他新权利的知识，又让他完成了登记，对吧？

sentences.en: Shortly after Amendment 4 was passed, the Republicans did come in behind it and they passed legislation that aimed to dramatically limit its effect.
sentences.zh: 第四修正案通过后不久，共和党人果然紧随其后，通过了旨在急剧限制其效力的立法。

sentences.en: See, I maintained my commitment from day one on this initiative that we would take this for what it was and we would continue doing the great policy work that I am proud of.
sentences.zh: 看吧，从这项倡议的第一天起，我就坚持我的承诺：我们要实事求是地对待它，并继续做好我引以为豪的卓越政策工作。

sentences.en: In June 2019, the Republican governor, DeSantis, signed into law a requirement that convicted felons pay all the court fees associated with their case,
sentences.zh: 2019年6月，共和党州长德桑蒂斯签署了一项法律，要求被定罪的重罪犯必须支付与其案件相关的所有法庭费用，

sentences.en: even a fee associated with accepting a public defender, before they would be allowed to vote again.
sentences.zh: 甚至包括接受公设辩护人产生的费用，才能重新获得投票权。

sentences.en: The argument was that a person's sentence is not actually complete until they've paid these fees.
sentences.zh: 给出的理由是，只有在支付了这些费用之后，一个人的刑期才算真正完成。

60万美元，好吧。

sentences.en: And, like, how much are you making a month, for example?

sentences.en: You're on a payment plan, okay.

sentences.en: That would be about 400 years before you'd be able to pay off the restitution.

sentences.en: Yeah, they know that.

sentences.en: So even though, technically, Amendment 4 gave Mr. Kelly his right to vote back, practically speaking, this new law made voting impossibly out of reach.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管从技术上讲，第四修正案让凯利先生重新获得了投票权，但从实际操作来看，这项新法律让投票变得遥不可及。

sentences.en: But then, shortly after Governor DeSantis signed the law,

sentences.en: 17 former felons, along with the ACLU, sued the state.
sentences.zh: 17名前重罪犯与美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）一起起诉了该州。

sentences.en: And in October of 2019, a judge said those 17 people did not have to pay fees in order to vote.
sentences.zh: 在2019年10月，一名法官裁定这17人无需支付费用即可投票。

sentences.en: And the expectation was that the ruling would eventually apply to all felons whose voting rights had been reinstated under Amendment 4.
sentences.zh: 大家的期望是，这项裁决最终将适用于所有根据第四修正案恢复投票权的重罪犯。

sentences.en: But in this moment, as we're talking to Mr. Kelly, everything is still kind of hanging in limbo.
sentences.zh: 但此时此刻，当我们与凯利先生交谈时，一切都还处于悬而未决的边缘。

sentences.en: While we're standing there talking to him, Julius comes over.

sentences.en: Yes, sir.

sentences.en: I thought I'd interrupt, right?
sentences.zh: 我想我该打断一下，对吧？

sentences.en: So, boom, I was going to come talk to you and ask you, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，轰的一下，我就来找你谈谈，问你，对吧？

sentences.en: And actually, that whole thing with the final restitutions, right?
sentences.zh: 其实，关于最终赔偿金的整件事，对吧？

sentences.en: On October the 17th of last year, a federal judge ruled it unconstitutional to deny you your rights to vote based upon monetary debt.
sentences.zh: 去年的10月17日，一名联邦法官裁定，以金钱债务为由剥夺你的投票权是违宪的。

sentences.en: They're still fighting it in the courts, but the states say, no, I can't vote.
sentences.zh: 他们还在法庭上抗争，但州政府说，不行，我不能投票。

sentences.en: The federal defense is not in charge of the election.
sentences.zh: 联邦辩护方并不负责选举。

sentences.en: Julius is trying to convince Mr. Kelly that he's okay to vote.
sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯正试图说服凯利先生他可以安心投票。

sentences.en: Honestly, right, I steal a restitution.
sentences.zh: 说实话，对吧，我偷了一笔赔偿金。

sentences.en: I just got my voter registration card.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚拿到了我的选民登记卡。

sentences.en: I'll go get out of the car and show you.

sentences.en: You can get a voter registration card, but legally you can't vote if you're a fellow in Florida.

sentences.en: But technically, Mr. Kelly is actually right that, for the time being, the judge's ruling only applied to those 17 felons.

sentences.en: And it just goes to show what a confusing tug of war this right to vote has become.

sentences.en: You know, I don't want to take that chance.

sentences.en: I understand.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: But thank you.

sentences.en: After this interaction, Julius is clearly feeling a little down.
sentences.zh: 这次互动之后，朱利叶斯显然情绪有些低落。

sentences.en: He says interactions like this can cause him to reflect on the nature of the work that he's doing and how he came to be doing it.
sentences.zh: 他说像这样的互动会让他反思自己所做工作的性质，以及他是如何开始做这份工作的。

sentences.en: What's it like trying to tell someone to go vote when they remember the same things as you over what the state of Florida once did to them?
sentences.zh: 当你想劝别人去投票，而他们想起了佛罗里达州过去对他们做过的那些事，心境跟你一样时，那是一种什么样的体验？

sentences.en: It's difficult, really.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: I really battle this thing inside of me sometimes, right?
sentences.zh: 有时候我内心真的很挣扎，对吧？

sentences.en: When I see a guy and he's like, man, adamantly against, like, voting in any kind of way, shape, or fashion, I have to, like, still persuade him to do this or whatever, you know?
sentences.zh: 当我看到一个人，他表现得像，天哪，坚决反对以任何形式去投票时，我还得硬着头皮去说服他做这件事，诸如此类的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And I used to deal with that a lot when I first got this job.
sentences.zh: 我刚得到这份工作时经常遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: Like, I felt like I was compromising my personal integrity.
sentences.zh: 就像我当时觉得自己在违背个人的道德底线。

sentences.en: Remember, Julius's main reason for taking this job wasn't his belief in the power of voting.
sentences.zh: 记住，朱利叶斯接受这份工作的主要原因并不是他对投票力量的信仰。

sentences.en: He took it because he needed a paycheck, which is really hard to come by if you have a felony conviction.
sentences.zh: 他接下这份工作是因为他需要一份薪水，而如果你有重罪案底，薪水是很难挣到的。

sentences.en: And while the passage of Amendment 4 was this moment where Julius saw what the power of voting can be, the legal battle that has ensued in its wake,
sentences.zh: 尽管第四修正案的通过让朱利叶斯看到了投票力量的展现，但随之而来的法律诉讼，

sentences.en: that's more closely in line with his overall experience of government and with the state of Florida.
sentences.zh: 这更符合他此前对政府以及佛罗里达州的一贯体验。

sentences.en: So while Julius makes a convincing case for voting every day at work, he can find himself being pretty conflicted about the work that he's doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然朱利叶斯在工作中每天都在为投票做着令人信服的辩护，但他发现自己对所做的工作感到相当矛盾。

sentences.en: As he's talking with us, he remembers one particular conversation where he really felt that, where another former felon actually refused to register.
sentences.zh: 在与我们交谈时，他回想起了一次特定的谈话，那次谈话让他深有感触，当时另一名前重罪犯竟然拒绝登记。

sentences.en: Young dude standing inside the middle of one of the worst neighborhoods on southwest side of Gainesville, Florida.
sentences.zh: 有个年轻小伙子站在佛罗里达州盖恩斯维尔西南侧最糟糕的一个社区中央。

sentences.en: And he was very well-spoken.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常能言善辩。

sentences.en: And I could tell from the look in his eyes and from the tone of his voice and the certainty of his words that he knew what he was talking about.
sentences.zh: 从他的眼神、语气以及坚定的话语中，我能看出他对自己所说的话心知肚明。

sentences.en: He knew how he felt.
sentences.zh: 他清楚自己的感受。

sentences.en: He knew why he felt that way.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己为什么会有这种感受。

sentences.en: And he was strongly against the government and voting and the whole system.
sentences.zh: 而且他强烈反对政府、投票以及整个体制。

sentences.en: I knew that he had an in-depth reason why, and I totally got it because I have that same view, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道他有着深刻的原因，我完全理解，因为我也持相同的观点，对吧？

sentences.en: I knew that he was awake and aware, and he knew maybe all the things I know, if not more, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道他是清醒且有觉知的，他了解的可能和我一样多，甚至更多，对吧？

sentences.en: At such a young age, I felt like, oh, man.
sentences.zh: 在那么小的年纪，我当时就觉得，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, man.

sentences.en: See, this young man here standing on his integrity while I'm compromising mine because I'm in need.
sentences.zh: 你看，这个年轻人在这里坚守着他的诚信，而我却在妥协我的诚信，因为我有所需求。

sentences.en: To be registering people to vote, you felt that was a compromise.
sentences.zh: 在帮别人登记投票时，你觉得那是一种妥协。

sentences.en: Yeah, I felt that especially in that moment.
sentences.zh: 是的，我特别是在那一刻有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Because you thought he was right.
sentences.zh: 因为你觉得他是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is, he is.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是对的，他就是对的。

sentences.en: And I totally got where he was coming from.
sentences.zh: 而且我完全理解他的立场。

sentences.en: There's a lot of people who will be listening to this that would say, I don't understand because the only way to change things is to go out and vote.
sentences.zh: 有很多人听到这里会说，我不理解，因为改变现状的唯一方法就是出去投票。

sentences.en: And I get it.

sentences.en: I'm not sure if you missed this news yesterday, but it's pretty monumental for us here in Florida.

sentences.en: In May of this year, the Florida judge who sided with the 17 felons and the ACLU did in fact expand his ruling to apply to all former felons in Florida.
sentences.zh: 今年五月，那个支持17名重罪犯和美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）的佛罗里达州法官，确实将他的裁决扩大到了佛罗里达州的所有前重罪犯。

sentences.en: Today, a federal judge called it a, quote, pay-to-vote system and said it was unconstitutional when applied to felons who were otherwise eligible to vote,
sentences.zh: 今天，一名联邦法官称其为所谓的“付费投票”系统，并表示当该系统适用于原本符合投票资格、

sentences.zh: 但确实无力支付规定金额的重罪犯时，是违宪的。

sentences.en: But the reality is that this legal wrangling could still continue here.

sentences.zh: 到目前为止，德桑蒂斯州长办公室仅表示正在审查这一裁决。

sentences.en: The state responded by challenging that ruling, which landed the case in a federal appeals court.

sentences.en: Major shakeup ahead of the election, a federal appeals court's decision today is now putting the voting rights of hundreds of thousands of felons in jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 大选前夕迎来重大变动，联邦上诉法院今天的裁决，让数十万重罪犯的投票权陷入了危机。

sentences.en: That court, the 11th Circuit, sided with the Republicans and allowed the restitution requirement to go into effect.
sentences.zh: 该法院即第十一巡回上诉法院支持了共和党人，并允许将赔偿金要求付诸实施。

sentences.en: Until they made their own decision on the case at a later date.
sentences.zh: 直到他们在日后对该案作出自己的裁决。

sentences.en: And thousands of Floridians are left in the lurch, unsure if they will be able to vote this fall.
sentences.zh: 这让成千上万的佛罗里达州人陷入了进退两难的境地，他们不确定今年秋天是否还能投票。

sentences.en: And just a few weeks ago...

sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，裁决称，想办法让重罪犯知道他们欠多少钱不是州政府的责任。

sentences.en: And the state says it would take years to make that kind of database.

sentences.en: On top of that, if a person doesn't know if they owe fines or fees and goes ahead and votes anyway, they could face perjury charges,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，如果一个人不知道自己是否欠罚款或费用，却依然去投票了，他们可能会面临伪证罪指控，

sentences.zh: 这意味着又一次重罪定罪，以及重返监狱的可能性。

sentences.en: Some estimates show that this could basically negate Amendment 4, that up to 80% of former felons in Florida will not be eligible to vote in November after all.
